correctness.rationale: For S=<a,a+h>, Sylvester F=a²+(h−2)a−h and symmetry yield G=(F−w)/p where w is the least element of S in F mod p. Writing w=ta+hy with 0≤y≤t yields the exact first feasible (I_r,J_r) at t≤p−1 when a>h(p−1); w<F follows from a>p. At residue 0, (I,J)=(p−1,p−1), unique among residues; a triple CRT argument rules out every alternate period d with p∤d despite admissible gcd(a,h)=1. Independent exact direct-membership checks matched 321 instances of p,h,a. The proof, not the finite checks, supports all parameters.
